title: The king as a fighting piece: bring it out only when it is safe
outcomes: Brings the king towards the centre when the queens are off and nothing can check it
Keeps the king at home, or does something else first, when queens are on and a check is available
Asks two questions before a king step: what heavy pieces remain, and what checks can the opponent give

steps.text: *The king as a fighter: pawn endings the active king decides* showed the king winning races in pawn endings. Most positions are mixed. Before you step the king forward ask two things: **are the queens (or rooks) still on**, and **could the opponent give a check after my step**? If heavy pieces are off and nothing can check the king, the step towards the centre is usually right.

**Rule of thumb, not a law.** Bring the king out when the queens are off and no check or mating threat exists. Before a king step, look for checks and skewers on its new square. A king in the centre is not always dangerous, and a king at home is not always safe; the position decides. Predict the next pair.

steps.title: Same ending, queens on: look for the check
steps.prompt: In the first position the queens are off and Ke3 is best. Now both queens are on, everything else the same. Predict whether the same king step is good or a mistake, then check the third position.
Before each king move: which did you check first, whether queens were on, or whether a check was possible?
